blocks.text: CEBU CITY, Philippines — Pedestrians here could face a fourfold hike in jaywalking fines as the city government eyes raising the penalty from ₱50 to ₱200. Local authorities said the proposal aims to curb unsafe road crossings, instill pedestrian discipline, and ease traffic congestion, particularly along the busy Banilad-Talamban (BanTal) corridor. The proposal comes after the Cebu City Transportation Office (CCTO) recorded around 4,000 jaywalking incidents along BanTal Road alone, which its operations head, Jong Alcover, attributed to intensified enforcement in the area.
